inputs.modified_text: They’re pushing changes to Cyprus’ surveillance laws that would strip away judicial oversight—the safeguard that might constrain whoever wants to monitor people. Lawyers are raising concerns, and the amended bill is expected to go to a House vote on Thursday. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides mentioned a recent closed session, which only adds to the sense that decisions about surveillance are being handled out of public view. This looks less like routine reform and more like an effort to make scrutiny easier to bypass.
